Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice E.S.Indiresh
 Oral Judgment
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

2. These appeals are arising out of the judgment and award dated 23.01.2020 in MVC Nos.88/2016,
89/2016, 90/2016, 91/2016, 92/2016 and 87/2016, on the file of the learned Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.XIII and IV Additional District Judge at NC: 2026:KHC-K:1056 HC-KAR AND 3 OTHERS Vijayapur (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal'), awarding compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.XIII and IV Additional District Judge at NC: 2026:KHC-K:1056 HC-KAR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Having taken note of the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties, these appeals are filed seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. In MVC No.87/2016 (MFA No.201677/2022), the deceased was aged about 58 years and taking into account the monthly salary of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority and as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the appropriate multiplier applicable is 9 and 1/4th of the income has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 10% of the income has to be added towards NC: 2026:KHC-K:1056 HC-KAR AND 3 OTHERS future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence,
the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,12,800/- (Rs.8,000+10%= Rs.8,800x12x9x1/4th)
towards loss of dependency.
5. There are five dependants and accordingly Rs.2,00,000/- (Rs.40,000x5) is awarded towards loss of consortium.
Rs.15,000/- each is awarded towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Accordingly the claimants are entitled for total compensation as under:
 Heads Amount Loss of dependency Rs.7,12,800/-
Loss of love and affection Rs.2,00,000/-
Towards funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.7,22,500/-
Enhancement Rs.2,20,300/-

 Heads Amount Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
Loss of earnings during laid up Rs.24,000/- period (Rs.8,000x3) Loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-
Towards food and nourishment Rs.20,000/- Towards attendant charges Rs.20,000/- Medical expenses Rs.43,810/-
Total Rs.2,07,810/-

Thus, the clamant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.83,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

7. In MVC No.89/2016 (MFA No.201019/2022, taking into consideration the injuries sustained by the claimant, global compensation of Rs.40,000/- is awarded with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from date of claim petition till realization.

8. In MVC No.90/2016 (MFA No.201048/2022), considering the injuries sustained by the claimant as per - 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:1056 HC-KAR AND 3 OTHERS Ex.P15, the award of compensation is reassessed as under:

10. In MVC No.91/2016 (MFA No.201063/2022), after considering the material on record, by taking into consideration the evidence of the treating doctor, the - 12 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:1056 HC-KAR AND 3 OTHERS disability is taken at 5% and accordingly, the award of compensation is reassessed as under:

Thus, the clamant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.65,833/- rounded of to Rs.65,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

11. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER I.
All the appeals are allowed in part.

II. The appellants in MFA No.201677/2022 - claimants in MVC N.87/2016 are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,20,300/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
